lesson.title: Standard VII: Protecting the Integrity of CFA Institute and Its Credential
lesson.summary: Standard VII sets two duties for members and candidates: behave honestly in anything connected to CFA Institute programs, and describe CFA membership, the designation and candidacy accurately. It matters because the credential only has value if exams are secure and claims about it are truthful.

sections.heading: Why a standard about the credential itself?
sections.body_markdown: Standards I to VI cover your duties to clients, employers and markets. Standard VII covers your duty to the **organization and credential** you belong to. Think of a university degree: if students cheat or graduates exaggerate what the degree proves, every holder's degree loses value. Standard VII has two parts: **VII(A)** covers *conduct* in CFA Institute programs, and **VII(B)** covers *references* to the organization, the designation and the program. Breaches can bring sanctions from CFA Institute, up to revoking membership, candidacy or the right to use the designation.

sections.heading: VII(A): Conduct in CFA Institute programs
VII(B): Referring to the organization, designation and candidacy
sections.body_markdown:
When you mention CFA Institute, membership, the designation or candidacy, you must not **misrepresent or exaggerate** what they mean. The standard aims at factual statements. It bans unsupported promises of competence or performance tied to the credential. Typical issues:

- **Linking the credential to results.** An ad may truthfully say that principals passed all three exams on their first attempts. It may not suggest this makes the firm's funds perform better.
- **Using the designation without the right to it.** A charterholder whose membership has lapsed (for example by not paying dues or filing the required annual statement) cannot keep using the letters until membership is reinstated.
- **Overstating candidacy.** Being a candidate or passing a level does not give you a partial designation. Say factually what you have done.

You may truthfully mention a volunteer role, for instance a committee seat. You may not imply that it gives clients a special advantage, such as inside knowledge of coming changes.

sections.heading: A simple way to analyse a situation
sections.body_markdown: Ask three questions. (1) **Is it about a CFA Institute program or the credential?** If so, Standard VII is in play. (2) **Does the act weaken exam security, confidentiality or the organization's reputation?** That points to VII(A). (3) **Is a statement about the credential true, and does it imply more than the facts support?** That points to VII(B). In a scenario, find the specific fact that tips it, such as a disclosed topic area, a lapsed membership, or a claim linking the credential to performance. Several standards can apply at once; the Code and Standards are meant to be read together.

worked_example.problem: Priya, a Level II candidate, just sat her exam. Afterwards she posts in an online forum: 'The exam leaned heavily on fixed-income topics, and one formula I expected never appeared.' Separately, she tells her study group which chapters of the official curriculum she found hardest to understand. Evaluate each action under Standard VII.
steps: Identify the standard: both actions involve CFA Institute exam preparation, so Standard VII(A) applies.
Forum post: even general topic areas and which formulas appeared (or did not) are confidential until CFA Institute releases them. Sharing them with the public discloses confidential exam information.
Check the exception: the forum post is about the content of a specific exam, not general study material, so the study-group allowance does not apply.
Study-group remark: which curriculum chapters she found hard is non-confidential preparation material. Discussing it with others is allowed.
Conclude: the forum post violates VII(A); the study-group discussion does not.
worked_example.answer: The forum post violates Standard VII(A) because it discloses confidential exam information. The study-group discussion is permitted.

exam_traps: Thinking only specific questions are confidential. Broad topic areas and formulas, tested or not tested, are also confidential.
Assuming study groups are banned. Discussing non-confidential material is fine; the violation is sharing confidential exam details.
Treating a true statement as always safe. A true fact (such as first-attempt passes) becomes a VII(B) violation when linked to superior performance or ability.
Believing a charter is permanent. If membership lapses, the right to use the designation lapses until it is reinstated.
Reading VII(A) as exam-day cheating only. It also covers rule violations, misrepresentation to CFA Institute, and using the association for personal gain.
leads_to: Applying all standards in integrated case questions

mcqs.stem: Right after sitting an exam, a CFA candidate posts publicly that one broad topic area was heavily tested and a certain formula was not tested. Under Standard VII(A), this conduct is:

options.text: A violation, because broad topics and formulas tested or not tested are confidential
options.explanation: Correct. Exam content is confidential until CFA Institute releases it, including broad topical areas and formulas, whether or not they appeared.

options.text: Acceptable, because only specific exam questions are confidential
options.explanation: Mistake: believing confidentiality covers only exact question wording. Topic areas and formulas are covered too.

options.text: Acceptable, because the post is available to all candidates equally
options.explanation: Mistake: treating wide availability as fairness. The harm is to future candidates and to exam validity, and equal access does not cure it.

mcqs.stem: Which action by a CFA candidate most clearly violates Standard VII(A)?

options.text: Discussing curriculum readings with a study group
options.explanation: Discussing non-confidential study material is explicitly allowed, so this is not the violation.

options.text: Telling a friend which formulas did not appear on the exam just taken
options.explanation: Correct. Formulas tested or not tested are confidential exam information, and disclosing them violates VII(A).

options.text: Reviewing publicly available practice questions with a friend
options.explanation: Public practice material is not confidential exam content. Confusing it with real exam content is the error here.

mcqs.stem: An adviser's brochure truthfully states that all of the firm's principals are charterholders who passed each exam on their first attempt. It adds that this explains why the firm's funds outperform. Under Standard VII(B), the adviser:

options.text: Complied, since every factual claim in the brochure is true
options.explanation: Mistake: judging only the truth of each fact. VII(B) also bans implying more than the facts support.

options.text: Complied, since charterholders are permitted to mention exam history
options.explanation: Mistake: the exam-history statement is allowed on its own, but the link to performance is the problem.

options.text: Violated the standard by tying exam history to superior performance
options.explanation: Correct. The facts may be stated, but implying that charterholders, or first-try passers, achieve better results exaggerates the credential's meaning.

mcqs.stem: A charterholder let his CFA Institute membership lapse by not paying dues or filing the required annual statement. He now prints business cards showing 'CFA' after his name, without reinstating membership. He has:

options.text: Violated VII(B), because he no longer has the right to use the designation
options.explanation: Correct. With membership lapsed, he may not use the designation until reinstated, so using it misrepresents his status.

options.text: Not violated it, because a charter once earned is permanent
options.explanation: Mistake: assuming the right to use the designation never lapses. It depends on maintaining membership.

options.text: Not violated it, because he is self-employed and not employed by a firm
options.explanation: Mistake: thinking the standard applies only to employees. It governs how anyone refers to the designation.

mcqs.stem: Warrenski sits on a CFA Institute technical committee and knows confidential details of draft standards. Which statement to prospective clients is consistent with Standard VII?

options.text: "My committee seat gives you an edge over competitors' clients."
options.explanation: Mistake: presenting a volunteer role as a business advantage and implying use of confidential information violates VII(A).

options.text: "I serve on a CFA Institute committee; this is a factual description of my role."
options.explanation: Correct. She may state her involvement factually, as long as she does not imply a special advantage.

options.text: "I will use what I learn on the committee to keep you ahead of coming changes."
options.explanation: Mistake: implying she will use confidential information for clients' benefit compromises CFA Institute's integrity.

mcqs.stem: A candidate knowingly gives CFA Institute inaccurate information about a matter connected to his candidacy. He argues that this did not affect any exam score and did not happen during an exam. Which conclusion is best?

options.text: No violation, because VII(A) covers only conduct during the exam itself
options.explanation: Mistake: narrowing VII(A) to exam-day cheating. The standard covers conduct in any CFA Institute program.

options.text: No violation, because no exam score was changed
options.explanation: Mistake: requiring a harmful outcome. Misrepresenting information is prohibited conduct regardless of effect on scores.

options.text: Violation of VII(A), because misrepresenting information to CFA Institute about a program is prohibited
options.explanation: Correct. Misrepresentation to CFA Institute about any program is listed as prohibited conduct, whether or not scores were affected.

mcqs.stem: A candidate has passed Level I and is registered for Level II. Which description of her status best avoids misrepresenting or exaggerating the credential under Standard VII(B)?

options.text: "Passed Level I of the CFA exam; candidate for Level II"
options.explanation: Correct. It factually states what she has done and her candidacy, without implying any part of the designation.

options.text: "One-third CFA charterholder"
options.explanation: Mistake: implying a partial designation. Passing a level does not confer part of the charter.

options.text: "CFA Level I" placed after her name like a title
options.explanation: Mistake: using the designation format for an exam result suggests she holds a credential. Candidacy must not be presented that way.

flashcards.front: What does Standard VII(A) prohibit, in short?
flashcards.back: Conduct that compromises the reputation or integrity of CFA Institute or the designation, or the integrity, validity or security of its programs (for example cheating, leaking exam content, or misleading CFA Institute).

flashcards.front: Which exam information is confidential under Standard VII(A), and what may candidates still discuss?
flashcards.back: Specific questions, and broad topic areas and formulas tested or not tested, are confidential until CFA Institute releases them. Non-confidential study material may be discussed, including in study groups.

flashcards.front: What is the core rule of Standard VII(B)?
flashcards.back: Do not misrepresent or exaggerate the meaning of CFA Institute membership, the CFA designation or candidacy. Do not make unsupported promises of competence or performance tied to them.

flashcards.front: May a firm say its principals all passed the CFA exams on the first try?
flashcards.back: Yes, if true. It must not link that fact to better performance or imply superior ability.
